key_insight: An Abaqus implementation combines strength-sensitive phase-field fracture with staggered displacement–damage updates and explicit enforcement of phase-field bounds and irreversibility.
engineering_relevance: Engineers can simulate brittle fracture nucleation and propagation using elastic properties, tensile and compressive strengths, and fracture toughness within native Abaqus elements.
method: Use UMAT and a heat-equation analogy to implement phase-field evolution with a strength-dependent driving force.
Coordinate staggered field updates through UEXTERNALDB, UAMP, MPC, and URDFIL.
Enforce phase-field bounds and irreversibility with a primal-dual active-set approach.
evidence_signal: The implementation is demonstrated on silicate glass using the “Nine Circles of Elastic Brittle Fracture” tests and native elements including CPS3, CAX3, and C3D4.
watch_item: The presented formulation targets isotropic, linear-elastic brittle materials with a Drucker–Prager strength surface; broader material applicability is not established in the abstract.
paper_title: Abaqus implementation of the phase-field approach to fracture
